Subject: Order Form — assurance clause gap & evidence sprint (security exhibit)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the updated order form. Our legal team flagged a couple of gaps in the security exhibit that we need clarified before we can sign:

1) Audit rights: the current draft looks broad — we need to confirm scoped inspection windows, sample sizes for evidence requests, and whether inspections can be remote-only.
2) SOC 2: we expect an annual SOC 2 report and a summary of any mid-year material changes. Is Redwood comfortable committing to delivering the latest report and a summary of changes on request?
3) Pen test: we need confirmed notice timing and whether the pen test can be performed by third-party vendors we engage. Also need to understand redaction responsibilities for any captured logs.

Attached: Seer_Health_OrderForm_v3.pdf (our markups are on page 5) — please propose suggested redline language for the exhibit and an evidence cadence that works operationally (we'd prefer a monthly evidence bundle for the first 90 days, then quarterly thereafter).

Can we have a short sync this week? Tom is flexible after 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement
Seer Health

Subject: Re: Order Form — assurance clause gap & evidence sprint (security exhibit)

Tom —

Appreciate the notes and the marked-up PDF. Quick response while we pull legal language:

- We can commit to providing the most recent SOC 2 report (Type II) annually and an executive summary of any material changes within 30 days of a confirmed change.
- For pen tests, Redwood permits customer-directed third-party testers provided there is a narrow test window, an approved rules-of-engagement doc, and a 30‑day notice. We will not allow destructive testing that impacts multi-tenant availability.
- Evidence cadence: we are open to your "monthly for 90 days, then quarterly" proposal. Operationally we prefer delivering evidence bundles via a secure Drive link with a short ticket for follow-up questions.

I've looped in Karthik (legal) and Laura (assurance ops). Karthik — can you draft two short clause options (minimal audit right vs. broader inspection) and a recommended redline for pen-test notice + R-O-E? Laura — please draft an evidence manifest template we can use for the monthly bundle.

Propose a 30-minute call Thu 3/11 at 3:00pm PT to run through the redlines and ensure we have alignment before Redwood legal sends the formal redline. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite + shared Drive folder.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — assurance clause gap & evidence sprint (security exhibit)

Tom / Kim / Laura —

I pulled together two redline options for the security exhibit. Below are the operative points (we will produce a tracked redline after you confirm direction):

OPTION A (Customer-limited inspection):
- Audit rights limited to: (i) receipt of Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II report; (ii) remote evidence artifacts (logs, configuration screenshots, compliance checklists) requested no more than twice per year; and (iii) a mutually agreed-upon, limited remote inspection once per 12 months.
- Pen-test: Customer may engage an approved third-party vendor with 30 days' notice; Redwood to provide a standard R-O-E and a non-destructive testing covenant. Redwood will not provide escalated access to production systems beyond scoped read-only artifacts.
- Evidence format & cadence: Monthly evidence bundle for first 90 days (items: SOC 2 summary, TLS cert inventory, access control list snapshot, recent deployment manifest, high-level audit logs) delivered via secure link. Quarterly bundles thereafter.

OPTION B (Broader customer inspection):
- Audit rights expanded to include on-site inspection once per 24 months with advance notice and reasonable limits on duration and scope; remote evidence requests up to four times per year.
- Pen-test: same guardrails as A, but customer may request limited vulnerability scans outside of the annual window subject to coordination.

Suggested legal text (short form for Order Form exhibit):
"Audit and Inspection: Redwood will provide Customer with Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report upon execution and annually thereafter. Customer may request remote evidence artifacts as set forth in this Exhibit in accordance with the agreed evidence cadence. On-site inspections, where permitted, shall be limited in scope and duration and require at least 60 days' advance notice and mutual agreement on objectives and personnel access"

Operational asks:
- Please confirm whether Seer requires on-site inspection rights (Option B).
- Confirm acceptance of the 30-day notice and non-destructive clause for pen-testing.

Attachments: pen-test ops template and a sample evidence manifest (two attachments). If we get an OK on Option A vs B, I'll submit a tracked redline for the Order Form and Security Exhibit.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PenTest-ops-notice-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Kim / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the two options. Seer prefers Option A with one modification: we need the ability to request an additional remote evidence bundle (i.e., up to three remote requests in year one) if we have a material change on our side (M&A or new product integration).

We accept the 30-day pen-test notice + R-O-E and the non-destructive covenant. For SOC 2, annual report (Type II) + summary of material changes within 30 days is acceptable.

I'll review your attachments this afternoon and follow up with a short set of inline comments in the Drive link. The 3/11 call time works — please send the invite and Drive access.

Appreciate the partnership — once we settle the small tweak, we can move to signature.

Best,
